    def route_load(r):
        s = 0
        for v in r:
            s += demands[v]
        return s

    def route_cost(r):
        if not r:
            return 0
        c = matrix[depot][r[0]] + matrix[r[-1]][depot]
        for i in range(len(r) - 1):
            c += matrix[r[i]][r[i + 1]]
        return c

    def total_cost(routes):
        s = 0
        for r in routes:
            s += route_cost(r)
        return s

            return False
        improved = False
        base = route_cost(r)
        n = len(r)
        # Limit search to keep deterministic and fast on large instances
        limit_i = n

            j_start = n - 1

                newc = route_cost(newr)
                if newc + 1e-9 < base:
                    r[:] = newr
                    return True
        return False

        ri = node_to_route[node]
        return ri

    def rebuild_node_to_route(routes):

        for i, r in enumerate(routes):

                node_to_route[v] = i
        return node_to_route

    # Kept deterministic by sorting with tie-breakers.
    unserved = set(customers)

    node_to_route = {}

def solve_cvrp(instance):
    depot = instance["depot_index"]
    customers = list(instance["customer_ids"])
    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]
    matrix = instance["distance_matrix"]
    nn = instance.get("nearest_neighbors", {})
    veh_hint = instance.get("vehicle_count_hint", 0)
    descriptors = instance.get("descriptors", {}) or {}

    # Deterministic helper functions
    def route_load(r):
        s = 0
        for v in r:
            s += demands[v]
        return s

    def route_cost(r):
        if not r:
            return 0
        c = matrix[depot][r[0]] + matrix[r[-1]][depot]
        for i in range(len(r) - 1):
            c += matrix[r[i]][r[i + 1]]
        return c

    def total_cost(routes):
        s = 0
        for r in routes:
            s += route_cost(r)
        return s

    def try_2opt_in_route(r):
        # deterministic first-improvement
        if len(r) < 4:
            return False
        improved = False
        base = route_cost(r)
        n = len(r)
        # Limit search to keep deterministic and fast on large instances
        limit_i = n
        if n > 140:
            limit_i = 120
        for i in range(0, limit_i - 2):
            if improved:
                break
            # j from end backwards tends to focus on larger edge exchanges
            j_start = n - 1
            if n > 140:
                j_start = n - 30
            for j in range(j_start, i + 2, -1):
                # reverse segment i..j
                newr = r[:i] + r[i:j+1][::-1] + r[j+1:]
                newc = route_cost(newr)
                if newc + 1e-9 < base:
                    r[:] = newr
                    return True
        return False

    def find_route_index(routes, node_to_route, node):
        ri = node_to_route[node]
        return ri

    def rebuild_node_to_route(routes):
        node_to_route = {}
        for i, r in enumerate(routes):
            for v in r:
                node_to_route[v] = i
        return node_to_route

    # Prefer a conservative construction: Clarke-Wright savings with oriented merges
    # Kept deterministic by sorting with tie-breakers.
    unserved = set(customers)
    routes = []
    node_to_route = {}
    for v in customers:
        routes.append([v])
        node_to_route[v] = len(routes) - 1

    # If we have lots of vehicles hint, keep merges slightly restrained; else allow more merging.
    # Not stochastic; only affects how aggressive we are.
    if veh_hint and veh_hint > 0:
